findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the claim 'review-bot and opcert have no reconcile path at all': autodeploy.sh HAS a review-bot source-change deploy/health/rollback path (deploy_review_bot); scope AC3 to the missing LIVENESS reconcile (restart a dead-but-SHA-current container), and confirm opcert separately has NO autodeploy path.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:1045 'docker compose build "$BOT_SERVICE" && docker compose up -d "$BOT_SERVICE"' inside deploy_review_bot()
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:1078-1086 'if changed_range "$bot_deployed" "$TARGET" "$BOT_PATHS" || changed_range ... "$SECRETS_PATHS"; then ... deploy_review_bot'
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:8 'redeploys the review-bot container IFF its source changed'
G-7a 'there is no X' frame refuted by Read
findings.finding: The plan asserts 'review-bot and opcert have no reconcile path at all', but autodeploy.sh contains a full review-bot reconcile/deploy path (deploy_review_bot(): compose build/up, /health check, :prev rollback, backoff) keyed on BOT_PATHS/SECRETS_PATHS. A source-change reconcile path for review-bot already exists; only a LIVENESS reconcile (restart of a dead-but-current container) is absent. The sweeping wording is empirically refuted and could cause AC3 work to duplicate an existing path.
findings.location: 'The defect' section ('review-bot and opcert have no reconcile path at all') and AC3
scenarios: AC3 implementer reads 'no reconcile path at all' and builds a review-bot source-deploy path that already exists, instead of the liveness reconcile the incident actually needs
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: 'review-bot has only a source-change deploy path (deploy_review_bot) and no liveness reconcile for a dead-but-current container; opcert has no autodeploy path at all.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the declared-service count: the compose stack is FOUR services (gerrit, review-bot, opcert, mcp) per compose-up.sh:284 — ensure AC1/AC3/AC5 enumerate opcert as a declared service the detector must cover.
evidence: infra/scripts/compose-up.sh:284 'compose-up: stack is up (gerrit + review-bot + opcert + mcp)'
infra/compose/docker-compose.yml declares services gerrit, review-bot, opcert, mcp
infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:1196 'gerrit, review-bot, opcert, compose-mcp-1'
Plan's own Observed block lists compose-opcert-1 as DOWN — contradicting the three-service claim
findings.finding: The plan states 'The system's three services are Gerrit, the rebar MCP server, and the code-review bot', but the deployed compose stack has FOUR services (gerrit, review-bot, opcert, mcp), and the plan itself names opcert as a dead service in the Observed/Summary sections. Undercounting the declared-service set is a false premise for AC1/AC3/AC5, which must enumerate what 'declared services' means.
findings.location: 'Why it matters for stability specifically' ('The system's three services are Gerrit, the rebar MCP server, and the code-review bot')
scenarios: AC1/AC5 'declared-but-not-running service' detection is built against a 3-service model and silently omits opcert — the very fourth service whose death the incident reports
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'three services are Gerrit, the rebar MCP server, and the code-review bot' with the four compose services (gerrit, review-bot, opcert, mcp), noting opcert is the fourth.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the out-of-file consumers a detectable liveness signal requires — observability.sh (publish_autodeploy_marker_delta) and monitoring_autodeploy.tf alarm — or record why AC4's signal is detectable without them.
evidence: observability.sh:1674-1707 publish_autodeploy_marker_delta wires '^AUTODEPLOY_* {' journal markers to CloudWatch metrics per rebar-autodeploy.service
monitoring_autodeploy.tf:28-200 defines the rebar-autodeploy-* CloudWatch alarms fed by those metrics
AC4: 'A liveness signal exists for the review bot such that its absence is detectable — today it is invisible'; the plan text edits only autodeploy behavior and names no publisher/alarm surface
findings.finding: AC4 requires a liveness signal whose ABSENCE is detectable, and AC1 requires autodeploy to 'say so', but the plan does not enumerate the two out-of-file consumers the codebase uses to make an autodeploy signal detectable: observability.sh (publish_autodeploy_marker_delta turns AUTODEPLOY_* journal markers into CloudWatch metrics) and monitoring_autodeploy.tf (the alarm on those metrics). A new dead-service marker/metric added only in autodeploy.sh would remain invisible without corresponding edits there.
scenarios: A new 'declared service dead' marker is emitted by autodeploy.sh but no observability.sh publisher/alarm is added, so the signal exists in the journal yet nothing pages on it — reproducing the original 'invisible' condition AC4 targets.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC4/AC1 an explicit edit surface: emit an AUTODEPLOY_* marker for a declared-but-dead service, add a publish_autodeploy_marker_delta call in observability.sh, and a paired alarm in monitoring_autodeploy.tf (or justify a different detectability mechanism).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve AC2's restart-vs-fail-loudly decision against the exit-127 root cause and record it, and if restarting, specify a restart bound/backoff (mirroring the existing BACKOFF_FILE/mcp-backoff pattern at autodeploy.sh:826-876) so a crash-looping service fails loudly instead of restarting silently.
evidence: Plan: 'Whether 127 is an ungraceful-termination artifact of the power cycle or a genuine entrypoint fault is NOT established — worth determining, because those need different fixes.'
AC2: 'It either restarts such a service or fails loudly. Decide and RECORD which; silently restarting a container that is crash-looping is its own failure mode.'
G6 approach-selection: the choice between restart and fail-loudly is a structural control-flow decision that the plan defers to an unresolved diagnostic.
findings.finding: AC2 ('restart such a service or fail loudly') leaves the restart-vs-fail choice undetermined because the plan itself says the exit-127 root cause (power-cycle artifact vs. genuine entrypoint fault) is 'NOT established' — yet that determination selects which approach is correct.
scenarios: If 127 is a genuine entrypoint fault (e.g. the observed clone/RPC failure), an unconditional restart in the no-op branch crash-loops the container every ~2 min; if it is a power-cycle artifact, a restart is the right fix.
A check-then-restart added to the no-op branch is a check-then-act with no restart-count/backoff bound (contrast the existing bot/mcp BACKOFF_FILE machinery at autodeploy.sh:826-876).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a proving command/fixture for each AC — e.g. stop compose-review-bot-1, run one autodeploy cycle, and assert the JSON log emits a distinct declared-service-DOWN event (jq -e 'select(.event=="autodeploy") | .service_state=="down"'), plus a second run with all services up asserting the quiet no-op.
evidence: AC5: 'Both branches proven: a healthy deployment still no-ops quietly; a dead service is reported.'
No 'Steps'/'Verification' section exists; ACs are outcome statements with no proving command
findings.finding: No acceptance criterion has a concrete proving command/check; AC5 claims 'both branches proven' but states no test, fixture, or command that would produce evidence.
scenarios: Reviewer cannot confirm the dead-service branch actually reports without a reproducible check
AC1/AC4 could be marked done with no evidence artifact
findings.suggested_fix: For AC5, script both branches: (1) kill a declared container, run reconcile, assert a structured 'service down' event; (2) all-healthy, run reconcile, assert 'no-op' and NO down event.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a probe step that reproduces/classifies the exit-127 cause (inspect entrypoint exit vs SIGKILL-on-power-cycle) and records the finding before choosing the AC2 restart-or-fail branch.
evidence: 'Whether 127 is an ungraceful-termination artifact of the power cycle or a genuine entrypoint fault is NOT established — worth determining, because those need different fixes.'
AC2: 'silently restarting a container that is crash-looping is its own failure mode.'
findings.finding: AC2's restart-vs-fail decision depends on whether exit 127 is a power-cycle artifact or a genuine entrypoint fault, which the plan explicitly states is NOT established, yet no probe/measurement step is planned to determine it.
scenarios: If 127 is a genuine entrypoint fault, an auto-restart path crash-loops
The chosen fix (restart vs fail) could be wrong because the cause was never tested

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the restart path's concurrency/idempotency: a per-service restart budget with backoff, and a guard against overlapping/successive ticks re-triggering a restart on a container already being (re)started.
evidence: 'journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy (runs every ~2 min, exit 0 each time)'
AC2 names crash-looping as a failure mode but AC3 ('review-bot and opcert have a reconcile path') does not state concurrency/idempotency guards for the new restart action.
Sibling cited in-plan: 'satirical-baryte-cat (worktree GC hangs inside its own lock and every later run SKIPs)' — a lock/lifecycle hazard the plan is aware of.
findings.finding: Autodeploy is a periodic reconciler (runs every ~2 min) that will now mutate shared host container state (restart) after a check-then-act ('is it down?' then 'start it'). The plan does not specify how concurrent/overlapping ticks or restart thrash are bounded — there is no restart budget, backoff, or ownership/lock discipline stated for the new restart path, so at-least-once (every-2-min) invocation could hammer a crash-looping container.
scenarios: Two autodeploy runs overlap, or successive 2-min ticks each independently observe 'down' and issue a restart, producing restart thrash against a container that keeps dying at exit 127.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the chosen mechanism and a positive rationale: WHERE the declared-service liveness check runs (e.g. the `up to date ... no-op` branch at autodeploy.sh:818-824), HOW declared services are enumerated (docker compose ps / declared service list), and why that placement fits autodeploy's existing per-component-marker design.
evidence: The plan is a defect report + AC list; there is no section describing the mechanism (e.g. WHERE the liveness check runs, what command enumerates 'declared services', how a restart is bounded).
G6 checklist item 4: 'The plan states a POSITIVE rationale for the chosen approach (its absence is a finding)'.

Grounding: the natural insertion point is the 'up to date ... no-op' branch at infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:818-824 (already runs mcp_retire_sweep/reclaim_under_pressure), and review-bot deploy machinery lives in deploy_review_bot() at 938-1071 — but which of these the plan intends to extend is unstated.
findings.finding: The plan states desired end-states (ACs) but names no chosen mechanism and no POSITIVE rationale for how autodeploy will detect/act on a declared-but-not-running service; G6 requires the plan to state why its chosen approach fits.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria (AC1-AC5) / plan has no 'Approach'/'Plan' section
scenarios: An implementer must invent the mechanism (add a check in the no-op branch vs. a new reconcile function vs. a compose-level restart policy) without a stated rationale, risking a solution that diverges from autodeploy's existing per-component-marker/backoff design.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a default for AC2 (e.g. 'detect+report only, no auto-restart until 127-cause known') and specify AC4's signal form (e.g. a heartbeat metric emitted on each webhook, absence alertable via existing monitoring).
evidence: AC2: 'It either restarts such a service or fails loudly. Decide and RECORD which'
AC4: 'A liveness signal exists for the review bot such that its absence is detectable'
findings.finding: AC2 ('decide and record which') and AC4 ('a liveness signal exists') defer real design choices to the executor without stating a default or the signal's form (metric/heartbeat/health endpoint).
scenarios: Executor pauses to ask 'which behavior?' or 'what kind of liveness signal?'
findings.suggested_fix: AC4: emit a review-bot heartbeat/liveness metric on webhook receipt so its absence (not just failure) is an alertable missing-data condition.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] For the declared-but-down arm, state the disposition contract in explicit retryable-vs-fatal terms: e.g. a first-seen-down service is transient (attempt one restart), but a service still down after a bounded restart budget is fatal/permanent (fail loudly / alert), never silently retried again.
evidence: AC2: 'It either restarts such a service or fails loudly. Decide and RECORD which; silently restarting a container that is crash-looping is its own failure mode.'
'Whether 127 is an ungraceful-termination artifact of the power cycle or a genuine entrypoint fault is NOT established — worth determining, because those need different fixes.'
No AC uses an explicit disposition word (transient/retryable vs fatal/permanent) for the down-service arm.
findings.finding: AC2 defers the failure disposition ('Decide and RECORD which') without pinning, per arm, what autodeploy surfaces when a declared service is down: a transient/retryable condition (re-check next ~2-min tick) versus a fatal/permanent one (fail loudly / alert). The exit-127 note explicitly flags this ambiguity (power-cycle artifact = transient vs entrypoint fault = fatal) but the ACs never require the disposition to be expressed in retryable-vs-fatal terms.
scenarios: A crash-looping container that autodeploy keeps restarting (masking a fatal entrypoint fault as if transient) vs a container down from a one-time power-cycle that a single restart fixes — the plan leaves which disposition surfaces to the operator unspecified.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Failure-disposition contract' line to AC2: e.g. 'first observation of a declared-down service → transient, attempt N restarts with backoff; still down after budget → fatal, emit a distinct loud failure (not a no-op).'

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.
